# NAMI

> Get mental health support, education, and advocacy from NAMI—the nation’s largest grassroots organization for people affected by mental illness\.

Generated by Yoast SEO v28.8, this is an llms.txt file, meant for consumption by LLMs.

## Pages
- [Homepage](https://www.nami.org/)
- [NAMI Ending the Silence](https://www.nami.org/programs/nami-ending-the-silence/)
- [NAMI Provider](https://www.nami.org/programs/nami-provider/)
- [Los Grupos De Apoyo](https://www.nami.org/support-groups/los-grupos-de-apoyo/)
- [NAMI Connection](https://www.nami.org/support-groups/nami-connection/)

## Justice and Advocacy Posts
- [Mental Health Education Policy: Model Legislation and Roadmap for State Leaders](https://www.nami.org/public-policy-reports/mental-health-education-policy-model-legislation-and-roadmap-for-state-leaders/): NAMI, the Mental Health Literacy Collaborative \(MHLC\), and Inseparable have launched a new resource: Mental Health Education Policy: Model Legislation and Roadmap for State Leaders\. This roadmap outlines ways to advance state mental health education, including existing state policy examples, and model legislation for mental health education policy that offers opportunities to advance mental health education efforts\. 
- [NAMI Regulatory Comment to CMS on Medicare](https://www.nami.org/nami-advocacy-actions/nami-regulatory-comment-to-cms-on-medicare-2/)
- [Letter to Congressional Committee Leadership on Medicaid](https://www.nami.org/nami-advocacy-actions/letter-to-congressional-committee-leadership-on-medicaid-2/)
- [Congressional Testimony on Mental Health Funding](https://www.nami.org/nami-advocacy-actions/congressional-testimony-on-mental-health-funding-3/)
- [Letter to Congressional Leadership on Mental Health Funding and Medicaid](https://www.nami.org/nami-advocacy-actions/letter-to-congressional-leadership-on-mental-health-funding-and-medicaid/)

## Blog Posts
- [Coronavirus: Mental Health Coping Strategies](https://www.nami.org/blog/coronavirus-mental-health-coping-strategies/): Acknowledging, recognizing and acting on mental distress in these uncertain times is key to lessening the impact\. Here are a few of our coping strategies to help those who may be experiencing mental health challenges during this health pandemic\. 
- [Coronavirus: Mental Health Treatment](/Blogs/NAMI-Blog/April-2020/Coronavirus-Mental-Health-Treatment): Social distancing during the coronavirus pandemic has led many patients and providers to quickly adopt alternatives to in\-person consultations\. If you need to continue or start treatment during this time, here are some mental health treatment options to consider\.
- [Early Psychosis Programs Are Changing Lives—But What if You Can’t Find One?](https://www.nami.org/blog/early-psychosis-programs-are-changing-lives-but-what-if-you-cant-find-one/): Until early\-psychosis CSC programs are available in every community, NAMI wants young people and their families to know what to do while we push for them to exist everywhere\. We can’t afford to wait\.
- [It’s OK2TALK about Mental Illness](/Blogs/NAMI-Blog/July-2014/It-s-OK2TALK-about-Mental-Illness): On Tuesday, July 23, the National Association of Broadcasters \(NAB\) launched their new “OK2TALK” campaign aimed at educating the public and encouraging youth to start a conversation about mental health\.
- [Hope is Within Reach](/Blogs/NAMI-Blog/December-2017/Hope-is-Within-Reach): "During my years of volunteer work, I have been constantly reminded that I’m not alone\. After struggling on my own and feeling helpless for a long time, I now know that there are so many people experiencing similar struggles\."

## News Posts
- [States push short\-term insurance as healthcare costs climb](https://www.nami.org/in-the-news/states-push-short-term-insurance-as-healthcare-costs-climb/): Short\-term, limited duration health plans may not help many people who have complex medical needs or need coverage for mental health care, says Jennifer Snow, NAMI's national director for government relations, policy, and advocacy\.
- [Federal judge rejects new Medicaid ‘frailty’ definition for work requirements](https://www.nami.org/in-the-news/federal-judge-rejects-new-medicaid-frailty-definition-for-work-requirements/): The ruling recognizes the fact that new requirements and subsequent disruptions to Medicaid coverage could have devastating impacts for people with mental health conditions and many others, said Jennifer Snow, national director for government relations, policy, and advocacy at NAMI\.
- [White\-knuckling the holidays: Why so many Americans put mental health on hold at the end of the year](https://www.nami.org/in-the-news/white-knuckling-the-holidays-why-so-many-americans-put-mental-health-on-hold-at-the-end-of-the-year/): Adults often write off mental health symptoms at the end of the year as holiday blues or stress, but it's important to recognize when the symptoms warrant a conversation with your health care provider, says Dr\. Christine Crawford, NAMI's chief medical officer\.
- [Why Your Mental Health Needs an Annual Checkup, Too](https://www.nami.org/in-the-news/why-your-mental-health-needs-an-annual-checkup-too/): Setting aside time to reflect on your mental and emotional well\-being can help you identify concerns early and start a conversation with your primary care provider, says Dr\. Christine Crawford, NAMI's chief medical officer\. 
- [NAMI and HMA Release Strategic Plan for Collaborative to Advance Innovation, Collaboration, and Action for Crisis Care  ](https://www.nami.org/nami-news/nami-and-hma-release-strategic-plan-for-collaborative-to-advance-innovation-collaboration-and-action-for-crisis-care/): NAMI and Health Management Associates \(HMA\) have developed a new strategic plan for the National Collaborative for Crisis Systems Innovation, launched earlier this year\. The Collaborative's strategic plan aims to turn concepts into action, organizing its work around awareness, access, capacity, and quality\.

## Podcast/Webinar Posts
- [NAMI Ask the Expert: Dementia Care and Support for Family Care Partners](https://www.nami.org/namis-ask-the-expert/nami-ask-the-expert-dementia-care-and-support-for-family-care-partners/): This presentation will provide family care partners with a practical and compassionate framework for navigating the dementia journey, drawing on principles from The Complete Family Guide to Dementia by Thomas Harrison and Brent P\. Forester, MD, MSc\.
- [Hope Starts With Us: How Lived Experience Shapes Innovation in Mental Health Care](https://www.nami.org/hope-starts-with-us/hope-starts-with-us-how-lived-experience-shapes-innovation-in-mental-health-care/): Access to mental health care services has grown over time, but there is still work to be done\. In this episode, guest host Dr\. Christine Crawford, NAMI’s chief medical officer, speaks with Sara Imtiaz, NAMI’s director of innovation, about how NAMI is working to increase access to care\.
- [NAMI Ask the Expert: Brain Donation — Why It Matters and How to Plan Ahead](https://www.nami.org/namis-ask-the-expert/nami-ask-the-expert-brain-donation-why-it-matters-and-how-to-plan-ahead/): Join Tish Hevel, founder and CEO of The Brain Donor Project, a nonprofit that supports the brain banks of the National Institutes of Health \(NIH\), for a practical conversation about why brain donation matters and how to make plans for yourself or a loved one\.
- [Hope Starts With Us: Helping Caregivers Show Up for Youth Mental Health](https://www.nami.org/hope-starts-with-us/hope-starts-with-us-helping-caregivers-show-up-for-youth-mental-health/)
- [Hope Starts With Us: Real Talk: Support for Athletes' Mental Health](https://www.nami.org/hope-starts-with-us/hope-starts-with-us-real-talk-support-for-athletes-mental-health/): At the start of the 2026\-2027 NBA season, five\-time All\-Star NBA player Kevin Love joins NAMI CEO Daniel H\. Gillison, Jr\. to discuss athlete mental health\. Rooted in his personal experiences, Kevin Love explores breaking the silence, moving past stigma, and finding help\. Throughout their conversation, the pair talk about what it means to identify as an athlete, the pressure that comes along with athletics, and his advice for student athletes\. Coaches, trusted adults, and student athletes will benefit from this open conversation full of Kevin Love’s lived experiences and his thoughts about how to best support young athletes\.

<style id="wp-block-media-text-inline-css">
/**
 * Breakpoints & Media Queries
 */
.wp-block-media-text {
  /*rtl:begin:ignore*/
  direction: ltr;
  /*rtl:end:ignore*/
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 50% 1fr;
  grid-template-rows: auto;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}
.wp-block-media-text.has-media-on-the-right {
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 50%;
}

.wp-block-media-text.is-vertically-aligned-top > .wp-block-media-text__content,
.wp-block-media-text.is-vertically-aligned-top > .wp-block-media-text__media {
  align-self: start;
}

.wp-block-media-text > .wp-block-media-text__content,
.wp-block-media-text > .wp-block-media-text__media,
.wp-block-media-text.is-vertically-aligned-center > .wp-block-media-text__content,
.wp-block-media-text.is-vertically-aligned-center > .wp-block-media-text__media {
  align-self: center;
}

.wp-block-media-text.is-vertically-aligned-bottom > .wp-block-media-text__content,
.wp-block-media-text.is-vertically-aligned-bottom > .wp-block-media-text__media {
  align-self: end;
}

.wp-block-media-text > .wp-block-media-text__media {
  /*rtl:begin:ignore*/
  grid-column: 1;
  grid-row: 1;
  /*rtl:end:ignore*/
  margin: 0;
}

.wp-block-media-text > .wp-block-media-text__content {
  direction: ltr;
  /*rtl:begin:ignore*/
  grid-column: 2;
  grid-row: 1;
  /*rtl:end:ignore*/
  padding: 0 8% 0 8%;
  word-break: break-word;
}

.wp-block-media-text.has-media-on-the-right > .wp-block-media-text__media {
  /*rtl:begin:ignore*/
  grid-column: 2;
  grid-row: 1;
  /*rtl:end:ignore*/
}

.wp-block-media-text.has-media-on-the-right > .wp-block-media-text__content {
  /*rtl:begin:ignore*/
  grid-column: 1;
  grid-row: 1;
  /*rtl:end:ignore*/
}

.wp-block-media-text__media a {
  display: block;
}

.wp-block-media-text__media img,
.wp-block-media-text__media video {
  height: auto;
  max-width: unset;
  width: 100%;
  vertical-align: middle;
}

/* `is-image-fill` is deprecated and the styles are kept for backwards compatibility. */
.wp-block-media-text.is-image-fill > .wp-block-media-text__media {
  height: 100%;
  min-height: 250px;
  background-size: cover;
}

.wp-block-media-text.is-image-fill > .wp-block-media-text__media > a {
  display: block;
  height: 100%;
}

.wp-block-media-text.is-image-fill > .wp-block-media-text__media img {
  position: absolute;
  width: 1px;
  height: 1px;
  padding: 0;
  margin: -1px;
  overflow: hidden;
  clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
  border: 0;
}

/* Image fill for versions 8 and onwards */
.wp-block-media-text.is-image-fill-element > .wp-block-media-text__media {
  position: relative;
  height: 100%;
  min-height: 250px;
}

.wp-block-media-text.is-image-fill-element > .wp-block-media-text__media > a {
  display: block;
  height: 100%;
}

.wp-block-media-text.is-image-fill-element > .wp-block-media-text__media img {
  position: absolute;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  -o-object-fit: cover;
     object-fit: cover;
}

/*
* Here we here not able to use a mobile first CSS approach.
* Custom widths are set using inline styles, and on mobile,
* we need 100% width, so we use important to overwrite the inline style.
* If the style were set on mobile first, on desktop styles,
* we would have no way of setting the style again to the inline style.
*/
@media (max-width: 600px) {
  .wp-block-media-text.is-stacked-on-mobile {
    grid-template-columns: 100% !important;
  }
  .wp-block-media-text.is-stacked-on-mobile > .wp-block-media-text__media {
    grid-column: 1;
    grid-row: 1;
  }
  .wp-block-media-text.is-stacked-on-mobile > .wp-block-media-text__content {
    grid-column: 1;
    grid-row: 2;
  }
}

</style>
